title: Quiz: Predictions and Residuals with modelr

questions.text: What does data_grid(diamonds, carat = seq_range(carat, n = 100)) produce?
options: A tibble with 100 evenly spaced carat values spanning the observed range
100 bootstrap replicates of the carat variable
questions.explanation: data_grid() creates a regular grid over the specified variables. seq_range(carat, n = 100) generates 100 evenly spaced values from min(carat) to max(carat). The result is a clean x-axis for overlaying a smooth fitted curve without the irregular spacing of the raw data.

questions.text: add_residuals(model) can be applied to a data_grid() output to compute residuals for the grid points.
questions.explanation: Residuals require observed y-values: eᵢ = yᵢ − ŷᵢ. The data_grid() output only contains x-values — there is no y column, so residuals cannot be computed. add_residuals() must be applied to the original dataset that contains both x and y.

questions.text: After fitting mod <- lm(log(price) ~ log(carat)), you call add_predictions(mod, var = 'log_pred'). The predictions are on the log(price) scale. To overlay them on a price-scale scatter plot, what transformation is needed?
options: Compute exp(log_pred) to back-transform to the price scale
No transformation — lm() always predicts on the original scale
questions.explanation: The model was fitted on log(price), so predictions are in log(price) units. To compare with raw prices, apply the inverse function: exp(). This reverses the logarithm and gives predicted prices in dollars.

questions.text: In the residual plot of the log-log diamond model coloured by cut, Ideal-cut diamonds cluster above zero and Fair-cut diamonds cluster below zero. What action should you take next?
options: Accept the model — the residuals are centred at zero on average
Add cut as a predictor to the model to capture the quality premium
Switch from log-log to a quadratic model
questions.explanation: Systematic clustering of residuals by a categorical variable (cut) is a clear signal that the variable explains variance the model has missed. Adding cut as a predictor will remove this pattern from the residuals and improve the model's fit.

questions.text: You compute the mean residual per cut level from the log-log model. Ideal cut has the highest mean residual (+0.18). What does this mean in practical terms?
options: Ideal-cut diamonds have the highest carat weight
The model overestimates prices for Ideal-cut diamonds
The model underestimates prices for Ideal-cut diamonds — they command a quality premium not captured by carat alone
Ideal-cut diamonds have the lowest price variance
questions.explanation: A positive mean residual means actual log(price) exceeds predicted log(price), i.e., exp(0.18) ≈ 1.2 — the model underestimates Ideal-cut prices by about 20% on average. This is the quality premium: Ideal-cut diamonds are worth more than their carat weight alone would suggest.

questions.text: add_predictions() and add_residuals() both work with lm(), glm(), and gam() objects, as long as those objects have a predict() method.
questions.explanation: modelr functions are model-agnostic — they call predict(model, newdata = ...) internally. Any R model class that implements a predict() method (which includes lm, glm, gam, nls, rpart, and many others) can be used with add_predictions() and add_residuals().
